title: ArrayList vocabulary
prompt: Complete the declaration and the size check.
explanation: Declare as the interface `List`, construct the concrete `ArrayList` — standard Java style. Collections use `.size()`, arrays use `.length`, strings use `.length()`.

title: The remove trap
explanation: An `int` argument selects the overload that removes by INDEX. To remove the value 1 you'd write `list.remove(Integer.valueOf(1))`.

title: Snapshot semantics
prompt: In backtracking, why `res.add(new ArrayList<>(path))` instead of `res.add(path)`?
options: `path` keeps mutating afterwards; without a copy, every entry in res ends up pointing at the same (eventually empty) list
explanation: Lists are references. Adding `path` directly stores a pointer to the still-changing list. `new ArrayList<>(path)` freezes the current contents.

title: Fixed-size lists
explanation: `Arrays.asList` wraps an array, so its size can't change: `set` works but `add`/`remove` throw at runtime. `List.of` is fully immutable (even `set` throws). Wrap either in `new ArrayList<>(...)` to get a growable list.

title: Remove while iterating
prompt: Two safe ways to delete every negative number from `list`.
explanation: `it.remove()` deletes the element `next()` just returned without confusing the iterator. `removeIf` takes a Predicate lambda and does the same loop for you. Calling `list.remove` inside a for-each throws `ConcurrentModificationException`.

title: Collect the evens
prompt: Return a `List<Integer>` of the even values of `nums`, in their original order.

tests.note: no evens → empty list, not null

solution.explanation: Create, filter-append, return. Returning an empty list (never null) is the expected convention.

hints: Start with an empty result list before the loop.
Inside the loop, `add` the value when `x % 2 == 0`; return the list after the loop.

title: Drill: pair up
prompt: From memory: return a `List<List<Integer>>` where each inner list is a consecutive pair from `nums`: [1,2,3,4] → [[1,2],[3,4]]. `nums.length` is always even. Drill the build-inner-add-outer motion.

solution.explanation: Stepping by 2 lands `i` on the first element of each pair. A fresh inner list per iteration matters: reusing one list would make every entry of `res` the same object. O(n).

hints: Build each inner list fresh inside the loop, then add it to the outer.

title: Strip and reverse
prompt:
Modify `list` in place: remove every negative value, then reverse what's left. Return the same list.

Use `removeIf` and `Collections.reverse`.

solution.explanation: `removeIf` walks the list once and drops every element matching the predicate, safely. `Collections.reverse` swaps from both ends toward the middle. Both are O(n) and in place.

hints: Two library calls do all the work: one filters, one reverses.

title: Recall: build & read
prompt: Fill in the create, append, read, and size operations.
code:
List<Integer> list = new {{1}}<>();
list.{{2}}(5);            // append
int x = list.{{3}}(0);    // read index 0
int n = list.{{4}}();     // element count
explanation: Declare as `List`, construct `ArrayList`; `add` appends, `get(i)` reads, `size()` counts (not `length`).

title: Drill: array to list
prompt: From memory: copy every element of `nums` into a `List<Integer>` (in order) and return it.

solution.explanation: An enhanced for visits every element in order and `add` appends, so the list mirrors the array. Each `int` is autoboxed. O(n).

hints: You need an empty list first, then one append per element.
`for (int x : nums) list.add(x);` — autoboxing turns each `int` into an `Integer`.

title: Recall: modify & query
prompt: Fill in the overwrite, remove-last, contains, and empty-check operations.
code:
list.{{1}}(0, 9);                 // overwrite index 0 with 9
list.{{2}}(list.size() - 1);      // remove the last element
boolean has = list.{{3}}(9);      // is 9 present?
boolean empty = list.{{4}}();     // any elements left?
explanation: `set(i, v)` overwrites, `remove(index)` deletes by position, `contains` scans (O(n)), `isEmpty` checks for zero elements.

title: Drill: overwrite the head
prompt: From memory: if `list` is non-empty, overwrite its first element with `99` using `set`; return the list either way.

solution.explanation: `set(i, v)` overwrites in place in O(1), but throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` on an empty list, hence the `isEmpty` guard.

hints: An empty list has no index 0. What must you check first?
